preamble: The voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] can lenite to an alveolar rhotic when the closure weakens and the place shifts forward. The clearest case is Romani, which rhoticized Old Indo-Aryan retroflex stops to r (and ř), so that Sanskrit ḍoma/ḍomba, the name of a caste of travelling musicians, became Romani rrom 'Romani man'. Most other Indo-Aryan languages instead keep the retroflex place and give an intervocalic flap [ɽ].

examples.from: Sanskrit ḍoma / ḍomba 'member of a low caste of travelling musicians'
examples.note: Romani rhoticized OIA retroflex ḍ, ṭ, ḍḍ, ṭṭ, ḍh to r and ř, one of the changes that set it apart from other Indo-Aryan languages.
